reviewer.actual_effort: I read each of the 36 listed band images once at its supplied resolution, and re-read s118-rows2. I could not zoom further or adjust contrast. I read current.json and the human snippets 1-7 file in full. I checked consonants, maqaf, sof-pasuq, periods, parentheses and rubrics word by word. I compared vowels and fine marks glyph by glyph as far as the bands allow. Below about 2-3 px, dagesh dots inside letters and short vertical strokes beside vowels could not be told apart reliably, and the items affected are listed under unresolved.

source_findings.correction: Accent marks are printed under the rest of the verse but are not encoded. What I can see at this resolution: a caret-shaped mark (probably etnachta) under the qof of בַּקֹּדֶשׁ; sub-linear accent strokes under the dalet/resh of נֶאְדָּר, the resh of נוֹרָא, the lamed of תְהִלֹּת and the ayin of עֹשֵׂה; a slanted stroke under the mem of the second מִי; and a vertical stroke (probably silluq) beside the segol under the pe of פֶלֶא. Which accent each stroke is (munach, merkha or tipcha) cannot be settled from these bands.

limits: This review covers only s116, s118, s120 and s122. The instructions about s110/s112 (bacharta, vehaadamah, leloheikhem, uvshokhbekha, the Deut 11:21 maqaf) were not reviewed because no s110/s112 bands were supplied and those pages are outside the stated scope.

I could not enlarge the bands further. Dagesh dots inside lamed, samekh and tav, and short vertical meteg strokes, are at the limit of what these bands show. Every such item is listed under unresolved with its exact word and letter. None is certified and none is rejected.

Across all four pages there is a recurring vertical stroke beside penultimate-stress vowels. It is the same glyph the human decision encoded as meteg in זִכְרֹנֵֽנוּ וּפִקְדֹּנֵֽנוּ. Except for those human-confirmed occurrences, the current text has no metegs on these pages. I did not apply the pattern to any word, because the instructions forbid inferring marks from other occurrences. A human needs to decide each occurrence from a higher-resolution crop.
I identified the accents in the rest of Exod 15:11 only as strokes that are present. I did not take any accent identity from the Masoretic text.
